text:
sam: spotted something during a spike: support team used the inspect flag for an embedding tenant and we got raw prompt text attached to a debug trace. not great. :grimacing:
raja: ouch. was that via the debug_elevate console flow or a manual flag flip?
sam: manual flip by a new SE, they toggled "allow_raw_debug" for one request and it propagated into the trace.
nina: that's our sweet spot for an accidental leak. we need safer defaults and a single-approval flow for raw-body access.
ashley: agreed. proposals: (1) make raw access require two console approvals (owner + security) and create a one-time encrypted artifact in audit-vault; (2) keep default logs to pseudonym fingerprints with rotating HMAC key; (3) limit raw unmasking to 24h and log every access w/ who/why.
raja: digging into infra: rotating HMAC keys is doable but we need to coordinate hash migration so previous fingerprints can be validated for older audits. Suggest key_version in fingerprint string: "fp:v2:<hex>".
sam: good call. also we should avoid keeping raw text in any persistent log stream. if we need it for support, it goes to audit-vault with envelope metadata: tenant, route, request_id, key_version, approver_ids.
nina: sample audit event (for discussion):
```
{ "event": "audit:raw_capture", "tenant": "tenant-42", "route": "/v1/embeddings", "fingerprint": "fp:v2:abcd...", "location": "s3://audit-vault/encrypted/xyz", "approvers": ["seq-id","sec-id"] }
```
ashley: access model: decryptable only with KMS-DECRYPT + CIDR-restricted worker + console RBAC admin. also emit an immutable access entry in the audit index (can't be deleted).
raja: sampling interplay: even fingerprint-only logs will be enormous for big tenants. we should use adaptive sampling: base rate by tenant_tier (free=0.001, paid=0.01, enterprise=0.05) but allow short bursts for incident windows. add circuit-breaker so avg tokens/sec threshold sets sampling=0 if exceeded to protect storage.
sam: example rule: `if tenant.rps > 2000 then sample_rate = min(0.001, base_rate/10)`; also add burst_tokens pool per tenant.
nina: console UX: show a per-tenant "raw-capture allowance" card with (status, last_captured_at, capture_count, approvers). but default should be OFF and the toggle flows into a modal that lists required approvers.
ashley: ops note: audit-vault retention defaults: 30d for hosted, 90/365 optional for enterprise via contract. encrypted artifacts auto-expire with lifecycle policies.
raja: we also need key rotation policy: rotate HMAC keys quarterly, rotate KMS wrap keys annually, and support a migration tool to re-hash historical fingerprints if required for a full-text search (very rare).
sam: what about embeddings linking? if someone has an embedding vector and a fingerprint, we should avoid keeping the plaintext in the same blob chain. store vector objects without textual copy, only reference fingerprint. make any re-association require vault-level access.
nina: runbook additions: 
- detect: alert when any log contains raw_body pattern or field request_body not matching fp regex
- immediate: flip tenant debug flag off + rotate ephemeral support tokens
- notify: page security + SE owner
- remediate: scan storage for raw artifacts and mark for expedited purge
ashley: operational constraints: some legacy customers asked for raw logs for debugging; we should map them to a dedicated "diagnostic enclave" offering with explicit SLA and legal checklist.
raja: next steps: (A) implement fp:v2 schema + HMAC rotation plan (owner: raja) (B) add console 2-approver flow + card UI (owner: nina) (C) adaptive sampling circuit-breaker (owner: sam) (D) audit-vault lifecycle + access controls (owner: ashley)
sam: can folks ack owners and delivery windows? ideally A/B/C in a 2-week sprint, D requires policy signoff from security/legal (P0).
nina: ack for UI, mockups by Thu.
ashley: ack for audit-vault design, will sync with security today.
raja: ack for HMAC work, will draft migration plan by EOD.
ops-bot: scheduled job: nightly-scan -> enabled. 0 new raw_body hits in last 24h. :white_check_mark:
sam: thanks all. let's gate any temporary console ability to unmask behind a feature flag and strong logging so we never get surprised again.
